Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Redacted]
Date of Birth: [Redacted]
Gender: Female
Admission Date: [Redacted]
Discharge Date: [Redacted]
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted following diagnosis of mucosal malignant melanoma of the hard palate. The tumor was found to have extensively spread within the hard palate with no involvement of the nasal cavity or nasopharynx, and with no neck lymph node metastasis.

Treatment:
The patient refused surgery and underwent CIR at another facility as the initial treatment, followed by concurrent chemotherapy. After one cycle of chemotherapy was stopped due to severe hematological toxicity. The patient achieved a complete response following CIR and was monitored by physical examinations, endoscopy, enhanced CT, and MRI. At 16 months after CIR, a cervical metastasis of a left jugular lymph node was detected, leading to diagnosis of stage crT0N1M0 MMMHN. The patient was treated by en bloc salvage ND with preservation of the accessory nerve, internal jugular vein, and sternocleidomastoid muscle. The duration of surgery was 132 min, and blood loss was less than 10 mL. The patient was discharged on postoperative Day 7.

Postoperative Management:
The patient experienced no Clavien-Dindo grade 3 or 4 postoperative complications. No recurrence was found by the whole-body enhanced CT performed 3 months after surgery.
Final Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-up Care:
Patient will continue to be monitored for any signs of recurrence or metastasis.

Discussions:
The patient was presented with several treatment options, including radiotherapy and systemic immunotherapy, before choosing surgery. The en bloc salvage ND with preservation of the accessory nerve, internal jugular vein, and sternocleidomastoid muscle was performed successfully, and the patient experienced no postoperative complications.

text:
**Suggested principal diagnosis code: C77.0 – Secondary and unspecified malignant neoplasm of lymph nodes of head, face and neck**

**Reasoning**

- This admission was for en bloc salvage neck dissection. The reason for it was a metastasis to a left jugular lymph node, found 16 months after the primary palatal melanoma had been treated with carbon-ion radiotherapy (CIR).
- The primary tumor had a complete response. The stage given is crT0, so there was no evidence of active primary disease at admission.
- In ICD-10-AM, a metastatic site is coded as the principal diagnosis when it is the condition treated during the episode and the primary is no longer under treatment. The lymph node metastasis is what occasioned and was treated in this admission, so C77.0 is sequenced first.
- The primary site is no longer present, so it is not coded as current malignancy. It is recorded with a history code instead: Z85.8 (Personal history of malignant neoplasms of other organs and systems). If your coding policy or the clinical documentation treats the primary as still present, the alternative is C06.9 or C05.0 (hard palate) as an additional code.

**Additional codes to consider**

- Z85.8, personal history of malignant melanoma of the mucosa. Some coders prefer Z85.8 here because the melanoma was mucosal rather than cutaneous.
- Z92.3, personal history of irradiation, for the prior CIR.
- Z92.21, personal history of antineoplastic chemotherapy.
- A procedure code for the neck dissection. In ACHI this is a block dissection of cervical lymph nodes, for example 31418-00 [Radical neck dissection]. Because the accessory nerve, internal jugular vein and sternocleidomastoid muscle were preserved, a modified or selective dissection code may fit better. Check the ACHI index against the operation note.

Final code assignment should be confirmed by a clinical coder against the full record and the current ICD-10-AM/ACHI edition.
